title: Tea and toast

clues.t: 67-year-old man, living alone since his wife died.
Gums bleed when he brushes his teeth.
Painful legs and swollen ankles.
Tiny bleeds around hair follicles on his shins, with corkscrew-shaped hairs.
A leg graze from 2 months ago still hasn't healed.
Diet is mostly toast and tea. No fruit or vegetables.

pearl: Not just a sailor's disease. It still turns up with restrictive diets, alcohol use disorder and in older men living alone. Symptoms respond within days of vitamin C replacement.

title: Pins, needles, pills

clues.t: 62-year-old man with tingling in both feet for 6 months.
Unsteady walking in the dark. Fine with the lights on.
Type 2 diabetes for 12 years, HbA1c well controlled.
Sore, smooth, red tongue.
Hb 128 g/L · MCV 106 fL
On metformin 1 g twice daily since diagnosis.

pearl: Not every neuropathy in diabetes is diabetic. Long-term metformin lowers B12 absorption, and neurological damage can occur before anaemia appears. Check B12 (or holotranscobalamin) periodically.

title: Salt of the earth

clues.t: 34-year-old woman. Exhausted, lost 6 kg without trying.
Craves salty food. Adds salt to her chips twice.
Light-headed on standing. Nauseated most mornings.
Palmar creases and gums look darker than her baseline.
Na 128 mmol/L · K 5.7 mmol/L
9 am cortisol 62 nmol/L · ACTH markedly raised

pearl: Hyponatraemia with hyperkalaemia is the tell. Raised ACTH means the problem is in the adrenal (primary), which causes the pigmentation. If she's unwell, give hydrocortisone before you wait on tests.

title: Slaughterhouse fever

clues.t: 38-year-old man with high fevers and sweats for 5 days.
Severe headache behind the eyes and aching muscles.
Dry cough. Chest X-ray shows patchy changes.
ALT 140 U/L · Platelets 98 ×10⁹/L
Lives in the Upper Hunter. Not vaccinated against anything since school.
Works at an abattoir processing cattle and goats.

pearl: Ask every febrile patient what they do for work. Q fever is notifiable. Prevention is Q-Vax, but workers need skin and serology testing first because vaccinating someone already immune can cause severe reactions.

title: After the dentist

clues.t: 63-year-old man with fevers and night sweats for 3 weeks.
Lost 4 kg. Aching joints. "Feels like a flu that won't leave."
He had a tooth extracted 6 weeks ago.
He has a known heart murmur from rheumatic fever as a child.
Thin dark streaks under two fingernails. Tender red lumps on his finger pads.
2 of 3 blood cultures grow viridans streptococci

pearl: Take three sets of blood cultures before any antibiotics. Splinter haemorrhages and Osler's nodes are late but classic. Prolonged fever plus a murmur is endocarditis until proven otherwise.

title: Dark on the windowsill

clues.t: 26-year-old woman with severe abdominal pain. Third ED visit this year.
CT, ultrasound and scopes have all been normal.
Anxious and confused this time. Her arms feel weak.
Na 124 mmol/L
Attacks follow crash diets. This one started after a new medicine.
A urine sample left on the windowsill turned dark reddish-brown

pearl: Severe abdominal pain with normal imaging, plus hyponatraemia or neurological signs, should prompt a urine porphobilinogen test during the attack. Fasting and many medicines can trigger attacks.

title: Slow burn

clues.t: 55-year-old man who has lost 12 kg over a year.
Chronic diarrhoea and bloating. Coeliac serology negative.
Years of migrating joint pains, long before any gut symptoms.
His skin has darkened and he runs low-grade fevers.
Now forgetful, with rhythmic jaw movements in time with slow eye convergence.
Duodenal biopsy: PAS-positive foamy macrophages

pearl: Caused by Tropheryma whipplei. Joint pains often come years before the gut symptoms. Rhythmic eye convergence with jaw movement (oculomasticatory myorhythmia) is pathognomonic. Very treatable with antibiotics, fatal if missed.

title: Barely a sting

clues.t: 29-year-old tourist with severe lower back pain that came on suddenly.
Drenched in sweat. Vomiting. Says she feels like she's going to die.
She was swimming off a beach near Cairns in December, 40 minutes ago.
She felt a small prick on her arm. Barely a mark there now.
Troponin rising

pearl: The sting is often trivial, then severe pain, sweating, hypertension and dread arrive 20–40 minutes later. Douse tropical stings with vinegar and call 000. It can cause heart failure, so monitor in hospital.

title: Hot is cold

clues.t: 45-year-old man with vomiting and diarrhoea, starting 4 hours after dinner.
Next day: tingling lips and fingers. His teeth ache, as if they're loose.
Cold drinks feel like they're burning his mouth.
HR 48
Three friends at the same dinner feel the same.
They ate a large Spanish mackerel caught on a trip off Queensland.

pearl: Hot–cold reversal is the giveaway. The toxin comes from large reef fish and isn't destroyed by cooking or freezing. Symptoms can last weeks. Advise avoiding alcohol and fish for a while, as both can bring symptoms back.

title: The night shift

clues.t: 49-year-old truck driver, exhausted despite 8 hours in bed.
Wakes with headaches most mornings.
Nodded off at the lights twice last week.
His partner moved to the spare room because of the snoring.
She says he stops breathing, then gasps.
BMI 34, collar size 46 cm, BP high on three medicines

pearl: Witnessed apnoeas plus daytime sleepiness is the classic pair. Untreated OSA drives resistant hypertension. Commercial drivers have specific fitness-to-drive standards in Australia.

title: Broken heart

clues.t: 66-year-old woman with sudden crushing chest pain.
It started at her husband's funeral this morning.
ECG: ST elevation in the anterior leads
Troponin raised
Coronary angiogram: no significant blockages
Echo: apex of the left ventricle balloons out, base contracts normally

pearl: It mimics a STEMI and must be managed as one until angiography. Usually triggered by emotional or physical stress in postmenopausal women. Function mostly recovers within weeks, but it isn't benign: complications and recurrence occur.
